title: Rice Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas)
content:
The yellow stem borer (YSB) is the most destructive insect pest of rice in India, causing 10-40% yield loss. The adult is a pale yellow moth. The larva bores into the rice stem, causing 'dead heart' at vegetative stage and 'white ear head' at reproductive stage.

Symptoms: Central leaf whorl dries up (dead heart at tillering). White, empty panicles (white ear at heading). Small holes in stem with frass (insect waste).

Favorable conditions: High nitrogen fertilizer, continuous flooding, dense planting, warm temperatures (>25°C).

Management: Clip seedling tips before transplanting to remove eggs. Use pheromone traps (8/ha) for monitoring. Release Trichogramma japonicum egg parasitoids. Apply cartap hydrochloride or chlorantraniliprole ONLY if ETL exceeds 5% dead hearts. Always follow label instructions.
content_hi:
तना छेदक धान का सबसे विनाशकारी कीट है, जो 10-40% उपज हानि करता है।

लक्षण: बीच की पत्ती सूखना। सफेद खाली बालियां। तने में छोटे छेद।

प्रबंधन: रोपाई से पहले पौध के सिरे काटें। फिरोमोन ट्रैप लगाएं। ट्राइकोग्रामा परजीवी छोड़ें।
summary: Rice stem borer causes 'dead heart' and 'white ear' symptoms. Monitor with pheromone traps. Use Trichogramma biocontrol.
summary_hi: तना छेदक धान का प्रमुख कीट है जो 'डेड हार्ट' और 'व्हाइट ईयर' लक्षण पैदा करता है।
actions: Inspect the field for 'dead hearts' — central leaf whorl that has dried up while outer leaves are green.
Install pheromone traps at 8 per hectare to monitor moth population — replace lures every 30 days.
If more than 5% dead hearts are found, release Trichogramma japonicum egg parasitoid cards at 50,000 adults/ha.
Clip the top 2-3 cm of rice seedlings before transplanting — this removes stem borer eggs laid on leaf tips.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer — lush green crop attracts more stem borer moths.
warnings: Do NOT apply insecticide during flowering — it kills pollinators and natural enemies of stem borer.
Cartap hydrochloride is toxic to fish — do not use in fields that drain into fish ponds.
